title: cuda: introduce graph-prefetcher and safe-rollback path for dynamic kernel migrations
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Background: we observe intermittent warmup regressions when CUDA graph capture occurs while the serving runtime is concurrently migrating kernels due to quantization/kernel-selection or when batch composition changes KV cache alignment. These regressions show up as flapping latency during the first 1-2 minutes after deploy and correlate with repeated graph re-captures that fail shape expectations.

Motivation: avoid repeated expensive capture attempts and provide a deterministic safe path that prefetches expected kernels and memory layout while still allowing fast capture when the workload is stable. This PR adds a small, opt-in "graph-prefetcher" submodule plus a deterministic rollback path for captures that detect incompatible kernel migrations at replay time. The goals are: 1) reduce warmup latency spikes for mixed-length continuous batching workloads, 2) avoid capture storms caused by transient KV alignment changes, and 3) keep fallback behavior explicit and auditable.

Summary of changes:
- runtime/cuda/graph_prefetcher.{cpp,h}: new module that probes likely kernel stacks for a target model signature and issues a lightweight pre-dispatch to allocate scratch memory, touch cuBLAS/cuDNN kernels and populate kernel->jit selection cache. Prefetcher does NOT perform a full capture; it only primes resources and warms the kernel selection path.
- runtime/cuda/rollback_guard.{cpp,h}: introduces a rollback token that is attached to a graph capture session. If a replay detects that the currently selected kernels or memory layout differ from those used at capture time beyond an allowed delta, the token triggers a safe rollback: the replay is aborted, the capture is tagged as deprecated, and a controlled fallback (immediate non-cuda-graph path for that request and a scheduled re-probe) is used.
- scheduler/continuous_batching: scheduling hints to prefer stable-KV-aligned groups for initial captures. New heuristics reduce attempts to capture on batches with high kv-misalignment ratio.
- runtime/kv_cache/kv_alignment_checker.{cpp,h}: lightweight checker that computes an alignment fingerprint included in capture metadata.
- tests/ci/gpu/warmup_prefetcher_test.cc: integration-level test that simulates shifting sequence-length distributions and verifies there are no capture storms and that rollback path is exercised.
- docs/notes/cuda-prefetch-rollback.md: short operator note describing new flags and observability fields.

Runtime flags (defaults conservative): --cuda-graph-prefetch=on, --cuda-graph-prefetch-threshold=0.25, --cuda-graph-rollback-strictness=moderate. Observability: every capture now emits metadata (prefetch_attempted, kv_alignment_fingerprint, rollback_reason).

Benchmark summary (local perf lab, p3.16xlarge-like):
- End-to-end 99th latency for a mixed-length chat workload reduced from 290ms to 240ms during initial warmup phase (first 5 minutes).
- Number of capture attempts per minute on synthetic unstable workload dropped from 9.2 to 1.1.

Implementation notes:
- Prefetcher uses asynchronous lightweight kernel launches and CUDA stream fences to avoid blocking the main inference stream. Prefetcher has time budget and will bail out if budget exceeded to avoid affecting SLO.
- Rollback path intentionally signals a deprecation tag rather than silently re-capturing; this allowed easier post-mortem and avoids oscillation.
- A small amount of additional telemetry is emitted; we added a coarse-grained opt-out via --cuda-graph-prefetch=off for customers concerned about noise.

Backwards compatibility: if cuda graphs are disabled in config, this module is inert. All new code paths are behind feature flags and default to conservative behavior. See release notes section below for operator-facing changes.

Related: ENG-9812 (warmup instability incident), ENG-9901 (continuous batching KV misalignment investigation).

b2d4f7e: wire prefetcher into capture controller and add time budget logic
c3e1a08: add rollback_guard and kv_alignment_fingerprint to capture metadata
d4f21b2: scheduler hints to avoid unstable batches for initial captures
e5b3c9a: integration tests and docs note
diff_snippets:

comments: Ravi Patel: Nice approach, avoids the 'capture thrash' we've seen. Two requests: make the prefetch time budget configurable per-model and add a counter for prefetch failures.
Ava Martinez (author): Added per-model budget and a prefetch_failures counter in follow-up commit b2d4f7e; documented in the operator notes.
Elena Kirov: Can we avoid racing prefetch with captures in the same stream? Concerned about interfering with priority scheduling on dedicated nodes.
Ava Martinez: Prefetcher uses its own non-blocking aux stream and fences to the main inference stream only at commit points; added a comment and small test to prevent priority inversion.
Jonah Wu: CI showed a GPU memory leak on the first run of the integration test; repro was a missing cudaFree in an early exit path. Patch c3e1a08 fixes this and added a sanitizer check.
QA (CI): warmup_prefetcher_test initially failed on mem-leak; rerun passed after fix.
bench_results: lab/2026-02-24: capture attempts/min 9.2 -> 1.1 on unstable workload
merge_details: merged via squash on 2026-02-25 by release-bot. Merge commit message: 'cuda: graph-prefetcher + rollback path to reduce capture storms and warmup latency (ENG-9812, ENG-9901)'. Changelog: runtime: improve CUDA graph warmup stability (operator opt-in flags).
release_notes: Operators: new flags --cuda-graph-prefetch and --cuda-graph-rollback-strictness. Default behavior is conservative and should reduce warmup latency spikes for mixed-length workloads. Telemetry: capture metadata now includes prefetch_attempted and kv_alignment_fingerprint.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-10012: long-tail benchmark under extreme quantization churn
ENG-10027: UI surfaces for capture deprecation events in Console
operator_notes: Operator guidance is in docs/notes/cuda-prefetch-rollback.md. Default flags are conservative; if you observe an increase in prefetch_failures or telemetry noise, set --cuda-graph-prefetch=off until next maintenance window.
